passage: Economists have long observed that people often value an object more once they own it. In one well-known experiment, participants who were given a coffee mug asked, on average, about twice as much to sell it as other participants were willing to pay to buy the same mug. Some researchers argue that this pattern reflects a dislike of losing things rather than any real attachment to the object itself.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: People tend to value things they own more than identical things they don't, perhaps disliking losses.
Researchers found that most people form a strong emotional attachment to objects they use every day.
People who are given objects as gifts usually sell them for less money than those objects are worth.
Economists have shown that coffee mugs are worth about twice as much as most people expect to pay.
steps: Sentence 1 states the pattern: owning an object raises its value to the owner.
Sentence 2 gives evidence: owners asked about twice what buyers would pay.
Sentence 3 offers an explanation: dislike of losing, not attachment.
The main idea combines the pattern with that possible explanation.
The text questions the attachment explanation, says owners asked more (not less), and makes no claim about what mugs are worth.
key: Include both the pattern and the explanation the text offers; avoid details that are only examples.
